pr_title: Add new display modes for accuracy counter
pr_body:
closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/9336

Increase display mode will show the accuracy that will grow from 0% (ACHIEVEMENT(+) in maimai)

Decrease display mode will show the accuracy that will decrement from 100% (ACHIEVEMENT(-) in maimai)

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34775378/210070059-4f11c9f9-13f4-41a8-8f04-ae08558bbcd6.mp4
pr_comments:
In the hopes that I can move this along I've ~~essentially rewritten this~~ applied a round of cleanups. @cdwcgt in the interest of making the review process of any future pulls you may want to submit less painless for us both I would like you to pay special attention to: naming changes applied, changes in xmldoc, as well as the test coverage added. Hopefully this should give an inkling of the standards we generally expect.

I've also fixed a stray issue that caused the accuracy meter to initially roll down from 100% to 0% in minimum accuracy mode (https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/21945/commits/6509d3538c203f41049218899b1dd0471dcfa385).

Going to need a second approve for this one. Not super sure about putting the new accuracies in `ScoreProcessor` as it's pretty central, but there is probably no better place for it.

issue_context.title: display maximum score/accuracy possible during gameplay
issue_context.body:
this should be a setting

the idea is that during gameplay, it shows the highest score/accuracy you can get if you hit everything perfectly

example:
let's say there are 100 notes in the map and i miss a note in the whole map
before i missed, the accuracy rating will read 100%
when i miss, the accuracy rating will read 99%, as the game will assume you will hit everything perfectly after that perfectly 

this can be used to determine the best performance possible when playing
comments: Definitely something we want to see added eventually.
I'm pretty sure the accuracy part was suggested before (#4638). I'll close that one as this one also includes score in its scope.
Sudden Death / Perfect multimod should also have an unranked third mod which will make you fail when max possible score/accuracy falls below a certain user-set treshold.

i think i also want to add max combo to the scope, if you miss something, the max combo possible adjusts and if you already got the max combo currently possible, then the max combo highlights orange or something

Hello, I'm currently working to solve this issue, ill like to present these 3 ideas for the UI and receive some feedback so that I can continue with my attempt.

![Test1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61520900/165683114-a6072869-3c4e-4424-90e9-d4435464d00f.PNG)
![Test2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61520900/165683119-2ebbfb90-7e06-449c-9ef8-44b823b03d8b.PNG)
![Test3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61520900/165683120-372e46e5-c8b1-416e-8633-cdc0d6feabb1.PNG)
.

First of all, I think it should be attached to the accuracy display itself, and be exposed as a `SettingSource` setting (see https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/17586 for an example of how this can be done), so proposal 2 best matches that.

I'm not sure "MAX" reads well, though. A potential alternative would be "final" or showing a fractional display

```
100.00%
   / 89.58%
```

I think as long as you structure things as proposed (inside the `DefaultAccuracyCounter` component) then we can figure out the speicfics of the UI in the pull request. Do what you think feels good to start with.
Actually I'm not 100% certain on putting it within the component. Unsure if players would want to put this display somewhere else on the screen. May be worth waiting for more opinions.

Another very strong argument is whether this should just be a setting on the accuracy counter itself. If a user wanted to show both, they could simply create two accuracy counters – one with each display mode.

i have a silly idea: instead of showing "maximum" accuracy, there could be a counter that starts counting the "inverse" accuracy from %0 to upwards, reaching higher counts as the user misses / hits 100s

If the counter was to have a display mode, that could also be added as a display method alongside the other two.

```
Standard (imminent accuracy)
Count up from zero
Count down from 100%
```

> `Nelite: in this case i see why "max" would be used, although maybe a better alternative would be to show the avg/max next to each other?`

Displaying it could be compressed using X%Y, X being maximum accuracy, Y being the current one or vice versa.
`99.75 % 81.75`
That can be done via the proposal I made above (https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/9336#issuecomment-1111787510). No further discussion is required for now.

review_comments: @bdach thoughts on making this something like "Count up" and "Count down"? It might be marginally more understandable to the end user.

I dunno, that seems worse to me. "Count up" or "down" relative to what?

Like yes it's true that the two types will only ever count up or down, but I feel that that doesn't really explain what the option means, especially when it's next to the "standard" or "current" accuracy or whatever.
To be honest, I'm not sure if anyone would actually want "minimum achievable" as a display mode. So maybe removing that then having "Current" of "Max achievable" as the only two options?

> To be honest, I'm not sure if anyone would actually want "minimum achievable" 

Its the primary ( only? ) display mode in atleast some DDR esque games so theres def precedent for it no?  i can see some people appreciating it as an option idk
Fair enough. I guess we'll go with the current terminology and see what the user reception is like.
